title: Trump Taps Hardliner Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff Following Midterm Debacle
snippet: President Donald Trump has appointed senior advisor Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff in a dramatic post-election shake-up, following a historic wave of Democratic victories in the midterms driven by public backlash over the war with Iran.
content:
WASHINGTON — In the wake of a historic midterm shellacking that saw Democrats seize control of both houses of Congress, President Donald Trump announced a major White House shake-up on Friday, naming senior advisor and hardline loyalist Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff.

Miller replaces Susie Wiles, who had served in the top post since the start of Trump's term. The staff upheaval comes as Republicans reel from one of the most lopsided midterm defeats in modern American history, driven in large part by public dissatisfaction over the military conflict with Iran.

A Democratic Landslide in Congress and Statehouses

As vote counting continues across the nation, Democrats have captured a decisive majority in both legislative chambers. In the Senate, Democrats flipped seven seats to secure at least 54 seats against the GOP's 44, with tight contests in Alaska and Mississippi still waiting to be called. Among the historic victories, Democrat El-Sayed was elected as America's first Muslim senator.

In the House, Democrats have locked in 253 seats compared to 162 for Republicans, comfortably crossing the 218-seat majority threshold. The party is on track to hold its largest House majority since 2008, with key contests still undecided, including Colorado's 4th District where staunch Trump ally Rep. Lauren Boebert faces a tight battle against Democrat Eileen Laubacher.

The election also delivered historic milestones in gubernatorial races nationwide. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history. Ohio elected its first female governor, Democrat Amy Acton, while Florida voters chose Republican Byron Donalds as the state's first Black governor-elect.

Administration Fractures Over Iran Conflict

Facing a Democratic-led Congress for his final two years in office, Trump indicated a willingness to cooperate on certain legislation while emphasizing he would not hesitate to use his veto power. Addressing the election results, Trump acknowledged that the military operations in Iran weighed heavily on Republican candidates, but defended his strategy.

"If I had to do it again, I'd have to do it again," Trump said on Friday, arguing that preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear capability remains a critical priority.

However, internal disagreement within the administration broke into the open when Vice President JD Vance attributed the party's electoral defeat entirely to the foreign intervention. In a candid post on X, Vance wrote, "The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. The reason we lost is the war."
